issues.description: The release contains documentation, seven substantial Stata programs embedded in PDFs, an online appendix, and four identifier-only CSVs (county, firm, judicial district and state); it does not contain the raw or prepared panels consumed by the workflow. Product-specific coverage/field compatibility and the named author-prepared intermediates remain unverified.

The seven substantial Stata programs are embedded in PDFs rather than supplied as .do files. Extracting/reflowing them and choosing a coherent working-copy root that preserves package-relative names are preparation; no exact author home-directory root is required. Only visually ambiguous wrapped lines need spot-checking during preparation.

Specific author-prepared producers/schemas are absent from the seven supplied programs: FBI_merged_district_ALL.dta (commented as created later), TRACdistrict_county.dta, fbiofficename_fbi_county_district.dta, personal_income_2000_2005_part1.dta and part2, district_prep_for_control_merge.dta, extract9203_renamed.dta, year_refer_all.csv, sum_whitecol_03_92_03_all_new.dta, sum_whitecol_03_92_03_all_bytype_new.dta, InsiderFeed hand-filled/geography crosswalks, and fbi_state_pop.dta. Resolve each named producer, input schema and order before execution.

P2 saves county_control_new_1990_2010_1.dta but later joins county_control_new_1990_2010.dta. P1 names fbi_office_distance_county_islam.dta while P5 reads fbi_office_distance_county_islam_treat5_forinsider.dta. P5 saves insider_fbi_stlouis_treat_90.dta but later appends insider_fbi_stlouis_treat.dta. Preserve these as distinct producer/consumer paths until a supported consistent route is established.

P6 uses after_new in the later treat_after_new expression although the earlier supplied block creates after_2002, and its year loop creates treat_year_* while a later local requests treat5_pop_year_1998–2006; intended aliases and definitions remain unknown. P6 also calls reg with absorb(state), while the Stata 18 Release 18 regress option table does not list absorb(). Resolve those command/variable intentions without inventing substitutions.

P6 writes state_treat_2.dta after dropping treat_islam_w_pop_state, which P7 later consumes. P7 also contains the literal command prefix reghdfe areg and restores reghdfe_first1, whose producer is absent from all seven programs. Resolve intended variable/object names and command structure without replacing the estimator.

P6 creates treat_after_new, saves/reloads the SAR panel, carries it into the prepared regression file, then issues a second uncaptured gen of the same variable after reloading that prepared file. No intervening drop or capture is present in the supplied path. Stata gen cannot create a variable that already exists, so this is a confirmed run-stopping source defect, distinct from the unknown after_new/yearly alias intent. No replacement expression is inferred.

evidence.description: README identifies the first treatment-building program and describes its judicial-district/FBI/RCMS inputs.
evidence.quote:
1. Generate data on FBI-level treatment variables 
File name: 1.Generate_treatment_FBIoffice_Muslim.do
Description: The code in this file links judicial districts to FBI offices through the common counties that they share using FBI office level data and the judicial district-county crosswalk data. It also creates a treatment variable at the FBI office level, 
and treatment at the district level by merging FBI offices counties level data and district-FBI offices with data from the Religious Congregations and Membership Study. The code also links SEC litigation cases to FBI offices' jurisdictions.

evidence.description: Datasheet states the TRACFED origin, FOIA context, subscription history, and author receipt of case-referral/prosecutorial-outcome data.
evidence.quote:
• The paper’s first analyses regarding changes in the FBI’s enforcement of white-collar criminal law
        violations are based on the Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse (TRACFED). TRACFED
        is housed at Syracuse University and obtains data on case referrals and prosecutorial outcomes
        by filing requests under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). Trung Nguyen, the author of
        the paper, obtained data from TRACFED through Susan Long, co-director of TRACFED, who
        is a statistician and professor at Syracuse University’s Whitman School of Management. The
        Stanford Graduate School of Business Library paid for TRACFED’s subscription on October 15,
        2015 while the author was at the school. Susan Long provided the author with the data on
        November 9, 2015. Harvard Business School, the author’s current academic affiliation, is also
        maintaining subscription with TRACFED, which allows the author to continue using the data for
        publication.

evidence.description: Datasheet identifies ICPSR NIBRS, WRDS Insider Filing Data Feed, FinCEN aggregate activity, and distinct Census/BEA/SAIPE/BLS/FDIC/NBER control-source families.
evidence.quote:
• In the second analysis of the paper, which looks at changes to white-collar crime, the main data
  that were used came from the National Incident Based Reporting System and Insider Trading
  data

    – Trung Nguyen downloaded data from the National Incident Based Reporting System, which
      are used for analyzing changes in wire fraud incidents, from the ICPSR website on May 2,
      2016.
    – The author downloaded insider trading data from Thomson Reuters’ Insider Filing Data Feed,
      housed at the Wharton Research Data Services (WRDS) on May 26, 2016

• The author downloaded data on financial institution reported suspicious activities from FinCEN’s
  website on October 24, 2016.

• The author downloaded control variables at the county level and state level, such as population
  density, percentage of the population living in poverty, median household income, the total number
  of divorced people, the population with a high school education, the number of banking and savings
  institutions’ offices, the amount of bank deposits, and the unemployment rate from the Census
  Bureau’s USA Counties Data File Downloads on April 5, 2017, which has collected the data from
  the Bureau of Economic Analysis, Census Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates, and Bureau
  of Labor Statistics – Current Population Survey, and Commercial banks and savings institutions
  – Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation.

• The author collected data on the number of people with ethnic minority identification and the
  total number of Black and Hispanic Americans from the National Bureau of Economic Research
  on April 5, 2017.

actions.description: Prepare a coherent working copy of the seven PDF-embedded Stata programs while preserving their supplied sequence and relative source names.
steps: Extract and reflow each of the seven named PDF programs into a working-copy .do file, keeping the original package-relative PDF path in the evidence record.
Choose one coherent working-copy root that preserves package-relative input/output names; no recovery of the author’s exact home directory is needed.
Spot-check visually ambiguous wrapped lines against the PDF pages and keep separate branch entry points in README order.
validation: Compare each reflowed program with its cached source text, then check only visually ambiguous wrapped lines against the PDF.
Confirm the working copy retains all seven source branches and expected package-relative paths.

actions.description: Resolve the named author-prepared inputs, producers, schemas and source-order gaps, keeping every filename variant distinct until the intended compatible handoff is documented.
steps: Obtain the named missing author-prepared inputs or producer specifications for the FBI/TRAC, district-control, referrals and insider crosswalk files; record field names and source years.
Resolve the unsuffixed/suffixed P2 county-control and P5 FBI-treatment/St Louis filename pairs against actual supplied producers and consumers before configuring any path.
Account for the state/year and branch order across all seven programs; do not run a consumer before its documented producer or an identified prepared-input route.
validation: For every read/save in the manual workflow trace, confirm an exact input path, fields and history from a supplied producer or compatible source route.
Review the complete producer-consumer chain after the intended filenames and schemas are documented.

steps: Resolve the P6 duplicate treat_after_new generation: the authored source saves and reloads the already-created variable, then issues a second bare gen. Obtain a supported decision about intended reuse/redefinition; do not invent a replacement expression.
Separately confirm the intended after_new versus after_2002 relationship and the generated treat_year_* versus requested treat5_pop_year_* names.
Confirm how treat_islam_w_pop_state is meant to reach P7 and which saved estimation result is intended by reghdfe_first1.
Resolve the literal reghdfe areg command and P6 reg-with-absorb calls from source/version documentation without substituting estimators or changing model definitions.
validation: Compare the exact P6 reg calls with the Stata 18 Release 18 Base Reference Manual; retain the authored estimator until its intended command is clarified.

After a supported correction and separate execution authorization, verify that treat_after_new is created once or intentionally reused, then check the remaining variables and stored estimates at producer/consumer boundaries.

review_notes: All seven embedded programs, README, datasheet, appendix, source/resource catalog candidates, file-level workflow trace, public route evidence, and exact runtime/add-on checks have been reviewed. No analysis_only scope is supported because the release contains no prepared analysis panels.

COMP.FUNDA was inspected as required by the frozen catalog instructions, but its annual product is not treated as a substitute for the author’s quarterly input; COMP.FUNDQ is only a readable local candidate, not a verified match. Public source pages are recorded as product-route evidence with compatibility left unverified.

An unauthorized self-written Stata probe (not author code or study data) was run: it fitted areg on four synthetic observations and returned r(198) for regress with absorb(). The probe is excluded from assessment evidence pending coordinator/root disposition; its do-file, batch log, empty stdout capture, exit-code record, JSON capture and invocation/cwd manifest remain preserved under probes/stata_absorb_probe*. The original outer tool-wrapper source bytes and separate stderr bytes were not preserved. No supplied author program or study dataset was executed, and no data were downloaded, software installed, or source edited. The reg/absorb assessment uses only the Stata 18 Release 18 manual and supplied source.
